name: Pointillist
oneLiner: 780 warm pastel dots, one per nonprofit client, assembled into a megaphone on pale peach.
concept:
Nonprofit Megaphone's proof is a count: 780 nonprofits, $48M in ad spend, 60 people, a 5% floor checked every month. Pointillist makes the count visible. The hero is a megaphone drawn from exactly 780 dots, one for each nonprofit client, on a hex grid aligned to the horn: small butter dots at the mouthpiece, larger apricot and blush dots at the bell, a rose lip at the rim, and a few hollow rings scattering off the mouth as reach. Your named account lead sits at the mouthpiece in a pill; a white card carries a sample month's click-through as a dotted line of twenty with Google's 5% floor ringed in cocoa at the tenth dot. Every other figure is counted the same way: $48M+ as 48 dots, the 60-person team as 60, the 100% guarantee as a block with every dot filled.

The ground is pale peach #FFF3EC, pinker and warmer than the paper and linen directions, and the ink is cocoa #3B2A25; four warm pastels (peach, blush, butter, apricot) belong only to dots, and one soft rose carries the primary button with cocoa text. There is no blue, violet, green, teal, red or black anywhere. Gabarito 800 gives the display a round, generous voice and Nunito Sans carries the body; there is no mono, and figures sit on dotted leaders instead of rules. The register is warm and hand-assembled but calm: plenty of empty peach, white cards with dotted borders and 14px corners, pill buttons, dotted rings around portraits, a three-colour confetti rule between sections, and motion that only ever assembles the dots from mouthpiece to bell and then holds still.
distinctFrom: Where Rings is one violet, a few large closed rings and pills on lilac, Pointillist is hundreds of small warm-pastel dots on pale peach that add up to a picture; the circle is a particle here, not an object.
bullets: A megaphone of exactly 780 dots, one per nonprofit client.
Pale peach, cocoa ink, four warm pastels for dots, rose CTA.
Every figure counted in dots; leaders, rings and rules dotted.
rightFor: Leadership that liked Rings but wants warmth over product polish, and a hero that counts its proof instead of claiming it.

palette.note: Pale peach for every page; pinker and warmer than Amplitude's paper and Signed Sentence's linen, and unclaimed by any other direction. Most of the screen stays empty so the dots breathe; the only texture is a 57-dot halftone fading out behind the headline's top-left corner, dropped on phones.

The 780 count card, the click-through card, the eyebrow pill, the ghost button, the account-lead pill, the letter stamp and the phone's letter card. Cards are 12-14px radius with a 2px dotted apricot border; pills are fully round. Shadows are soft (18/40px at 35% cocoa with negative spread) so cards float on the peach rather than sit.

Warm dark cocoa for headlines, body, figures, the mark disc, the 5% floor ring and pointer, the hover ring on rose buttons and the focus outline. 12.5:1 on peach, 13.6:1 on white, 5.6:1 on rose; never pure black.
Labels, captions, units, the fine print, the client-roll label and the small card copy. 5.4:1 on peach and 5.8:1 on white, so every 11px label passes AA. Never used on rose (2.4:1).

The mid-horn dots, the halftone behind the headline, the eyebrow's dotted border, the first colour of the confetti rule and the client-roll separators. Butter #F9DE8A is the fifth pastel: mouthpiece dots, the 100% stat block and the SAMPLE MONTH tag's dotted border. Pastels are dots, borders and fills only; they never carry text.

The bell dots, the $48M+ block, the twenty-dot click-through line, every dotted leader, the dotted card borders, the dotted underline beneath 'click by click.' and the account lead's ring. 1.8:1 on white, so it borders cards, never controls.
The dots nearest the rim, the 60+ team block, the account-lead pill's border, the phone letter card's border, Amber Snow's placeholder disc and the third colour of the confetti rule.

The one surface that carries text: primary buttons with cocoa labels (5.6:1), plus the rim lip of the megaphone, the eyebrow's third dot, the active-nav dot and the letter seal. Pressed buttons deepen to #E07F94 (cocoa 4.7:1); hover adds a dotted cocoa ring 3px outside the pill instead of changing the fill. Never text, never a background under body copy.

typography.display: Gabarito (Google Fonts): 800 for h1, the 780 count, the click-through figure and the three stat figures; 700 for the wordmark and the Michelle Hurtado quote. Its round bowls, open counters and single-storey a rhyme with the dots; never used below 14px.
typography.body: Nunito Sans (Google Fonts): 400 body, 500 nav links, captions, units and fine print, 600 buttons, labels, eyebrows, tags and inline emphasis. Two families total, loaded from fonts.googleapis.com only; no Fontshare, no self-hosting, no mono.
typography.scaleNotes: Desktop h1 60px / .98 / -.025em in two lines ('$10,000 a month,' / 'click by click.'), sentence case, cocoa only; instead of a coloured phrase the second line sits on a row of apricot dots. Count figure 32px Gabarito 800; click-through figure 24px; stat figures 26px; quote 19px Gabarito 700. Body 18px / 1.5 at max-width 470px; guarantee 15px; card copy 12-13px; fine print 12px Nunito Sans 500. Labels, eyebrows and tags are 11px Nunito Sans 600, uppercase, .06-.1em tracking; 11px is the floor and nothing is set below it. Phone: h1 36px / 1.0, count 28px, click-through 22px, body 16px / 1.5, quote 16px. Buttons are pills: 56px in the desktop hero (44px nav), 52px phone primary, 48px phone secondary, 36px phone nav; time tags are 30px and 28px dotted pills at 11px. Spacing on an 8px base: nav 80, hero 590, trust 182 on desktop (frame 852px); nav 60 on the phone. Every figure carries a unit, and the click-through carries SAMPLE MONTH until a consented account replaces it.

layout:
- Grid: 12 columns, 1200px container, 48px gutters at desktop, 24px tablet, 16px phone; vertical rhythm on 8px. Sections are separated by a confetti rule (peach, apricot and blush dots at 10px pitch) and a section number inside a 32px dotted ring (01, 02, 03). A dot figure (the megaphone, a stat block, a dot line) appears at most once per screen so the device stays special.
- 00 Nav (80px, no rule): cocoa disc mark holding a six-dot cone + 'Nonprofit Megaphone' Gabarito 700 with an 11px 'Google Ad Grant management' line; Services, Our work, Happy clients, Team, Blog as plain links, the active one carrying a rose dot beneath; 'Get a free quote' with a dotted apricot underline on hover; 'Book a free call' rose pill with the three-dot glyph. Past the hero the nav gains a white background and the CTA compresses to glyph + 'Book'.
- 01 Hero (590px; 560px copy column, 640px field): a 57-dot peach halftone fading out behind the top-left corner; eyebrow pill 'One of Google's first nine certified agencies' with three dots (butter, apricot, rose); h1 '$10,000 a month, / click by click.' with the second line on a row of apricot dots; sub naming the $10,000, the click as a person and the 5% floor; action row = rose 'Book a free call · 15 min' pill + white 'Am I eligible? · 2 min' pill with a dotted-ring icon; fine print with pastel dot separators; guarantee row with Amber Snow's portrait in a dotted rose ring, 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy' and 'Read the guarantee'. Field: the 780-dot megaphone (543 x 447px, 28 degrees up-right, dots 3.4px at the mouthpiece to 5.5px at the bell, eight colour bands from butter to rose with 7% speckle, nine hollow rings scattering off the bell); the '780 dots, one each' card top left; the account-lead pill at the mouthpiece bottom left; the click-through card bottom right (SAMPLE MONTH tag, 'Kept above the floor ····· 8.4%', twenty dots with the tenth ringed in cocoa, 'Google's 5% floor', 'Two months under it and Google can deactivate the account'). Reading order: count, lead, click-through.
- 02 Trust strip (confetti rule above, 182px): letter seal (white disc, dotted rose ring, rose centre), 'Letter from Google · Michelle Hurtado, first Head of Ad Grants', the quote in 19px Gabarito 700; three counted stats as SVG dot blocks over Gabarito 800 figures: $48M+ 'one dot per $1M' (48 apricot dots), 60+ 'one dot each' (60 blush dots), 100% 'every dot filled' (100 butter dots); the client roll 'Among 780+ clients · Sep 2026' with UNCF, Scouting America, COPD Foundation, YWCA Chicago, Earthwatch, Solar Sister, AAU, JFCS between pastel dots.
- 03 The rules (policy literacy): Google's seven requirements as a dotted list, each row a white card with a dot state (filled apricot = we handle it, ringed cocoa = the one with a deadline) and requirement / what Google does if you miss it / what we do about it, covering 5% CTR, conversion tracking, single-word keywords, account structure, monthly login, geo-targeting, quality score; the CTR row repeats the twenty-dot line; dated source link to Google's policy page.
- 04 Eligibility checker (rep-free exit): three questions as pill toggles (org type, country, working website) beside a ring of twelve dots that fills four per answer; a full ring offers the call; hospitals, schools and governments get an honest 'not eligible, here's why' card quoting Google's definition.
- 05 Outcomes: twelve case files as soft-cornered cards with dotted borders (wordmark, vertical, twelve-month period, one dot-line figure) with filter pills for the 12 verticals; each opens a case file with input, outcome, period, source, 'Open case file' and 'Forward to board (PDF)'. Every figure is verified with the client before launch.
- 06 What it costs: a flat monthly fee stated in one sentence if leadership approves it, never a percentage of spend; the seven services as dot blocks sized to their share of a typical engagement, Ad Grant management largest (Ad Grant management, Website SEO, Content creation, VisitorEmail, Google Remarketing, Microsoft Advertising, Spanish ad creation).
- 07 One of nine (contained white band with 16px corners and a dotted border, not full-bleed): the inaugural Google Ad Grants Certified Professional fact as text inside a dotted ring, the Google Partner badge with its clear-space rules, Inc. 5000 x4 as dotted seals; nine dots with one ringed as the section mark.
- 08 Your team, named: six to eight circular colour portraits in dotted pastel rings on a loose dot grid around a 'your account lead' portrait; role and 'Nonprofits I support' captions; the cabin-retreat candid cropped in one large dotted ring; copy stating who the prospect's named contact will be.
- 09 Reporting, shown: a real monthly report rendered as dot lines with a named client and month: spend as 100 dots of $100, click-through as the twenty-dot line with the floor ringed, compliance as filled versus hollow dots (no green exists in the system); beside it the one-sentence month signed by the account lead with a ringed portrait and date.
- 10 Guarantee band (white, dotted border, contained): the $25 CEO guarantee in 52px Gabarito 800, Amber Snow's portrait in a dotted rose ring, 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy', one rose pill.
- 11 FAQ: five plain-language questions as cards that expand (why pay for something free; will it raise money, answered honestly; who is on my account; what if we get suspended; how long to acquire), each with a dated source where a policy is cited.
- 12 Final CTA row: the hero action pair repeated verbatim plus 'See a real account report' link opening a redacted PDF.
- 13 Footer: four columns, social icons in dotted rings, a pill newsletter input, address, client-login link; 780+ used consistently; print stylesheet for case files and the guarantee page.
imagery: No illustration system and no stock photography. Four image types only. First, the dot figures: the megaphone is 780 inline SVG circles generated from a small token set (shape, pitch 12px desktop and 5.6px phone, dot radius 3.4-5.5px, eight bands, five pastels with 7% speckle, rose only on the rim) so the count is a literal number in the markup and a script regenerates the figure when the client count changes; the stat blocks are SVG patterns whose rectangle is the count (72 x 24px at a 6px pitch is 48 dots); the click-through line is twenty circles with the tenth ringed. Second, photography of NPM's people in circular crops inside dotted rings only: colour, eye-level, shot on a plain peach backdrop so the crop reads as a disc; Amber Snow and the account lead in the hero (CSS placeholder discs with role='img' labels until the shoot), six to eight team portraits below the fold. Third, real screens: the monthly report re-rendered as dot lines with a named client, month and visible SAMPLE or REDACTED pills, never blur. Fourth, badges and clients as typography: wordmarks in Nunito Sans 500 between pastel dots, the certification as text inside a dotted ring, Inc. 5000 as dotted seals, so no logo licensing is needed. Iconography is dots only: a cocoa disc with a six-dot cone for the mark, a growing three-dot glyph on rose buttons, a dotted ring with a centre dot for eligibility, a 2 x 2 of dots for the menu. Data viz: peach ground, apricot series one, blush series two, cocoa rings for thresholds, dotted leaders for labels, a unit and a period on every chart, and Google's 5% floor ringed wherever click-through is charted.
motion: Static first; the assembled megaphone is the design and nothing depends on JavaScript. 1. Hero load (pure CSS, shipped in the mockup): the eight dot bands settle from 55% scale and zero opacity, mouthpiece first and bell last at 100ms intervals over about 1.2s, so the horn fills the way sound travels; the scatter rings fade in at 1.15s; the halftone behind the headline fades in; the count card, the lead pill and the click-through card pop up 8px with a stagger; the cocoa floor ring fades in last. Copy is readable from frame one. 2. Phone: the same bands settle 80ms apart at the smaller scale, then the two cards pop. 3. Hover: rose buttons gain a dotted cocoa ring 3px outside the pill; the ghost button's dots turn solid cocoa; nav links grow a rose dot beneath; the quote and guarantee links carry dotted apricot underlines; pressed buttons deepen to #E07F94. 4. Below the fold (optional GSAP + ScrollTrigger sprint, native scroll only, no Lenis, JS budget under 300kB): stat blocks fill dot by dot at 30% in view, the eligibility ring gains four dots per answer, report lines draw left to right, FAQ cards expand. 5. prefers-reduced-motion: every keyframe lives inside a no-preference media query, so reduced-motion users get the finished megaphone and cards with zero keyframes. Nothing loops. 6. Never: WebGL, particle systems that never settle, kinetic type, parallax on portraits, autoplaying video, scroll-jacking, or dots that move on scroll.
mobile: The 390px hero is its own composition, not the field shrunk. Nav (60px): 34px cocoa disc mark, 'Nonprofit Megaphone' 14px Gabarito 700, a 36px rose 'Book a call' pill and a 40px white menu disc with a dotted border and a 2 x 2 dot icon. Hero (16px gutters): 'Certified by Google · one of the first nine' eyebrow pill; h1 36px in two lines ('$10,000 a month,' / 'click by click.') on the dotted underline; then a 200px figure: the same 780 dots regenerated at a 5.6px pitch and a flatter 14-degree angle sitting right, with the '780 dots, one each' card at top left; then a full-width white card with the sample-month click-through: SAMPLE MONTH tag, 'Click-through ····· 8.4%', the twenty-dot line with the 5% floor ringed, and 'Google's 5% floor · two misses in a row and Google can deactivate'. Then a four-line sub, a full-width 52px rose 'Book a free call · 15 min' pill and a full-width 48px white 'Am I eligible? · 2 min' pill (a button, not a text link), and a centred fine-print line with dot separators. The primary CTA sits at about 636px and the eligibility button at about 698px, both inside a 760px fold. One trust element follows: the Letter from Google as a soft white card with a dotted blush border, the seal, the quote at 16px Gabarito 700 and 'Letter from Google · Michelle Hurtado, first Head of Ad Grants'. Below the fold the stat blocks become a row of three, the client roll wraps to two dotted lines, the rules become a dotted list, outcome cards go two-up, and team portraits sit in a two-column grid of dotted rings. Tap targets are 44px minimum; the account-lead pill and the headline halftone are dropped on phones; the corner confetti shrinks to three dots.
a11y: Target WCAG 2.2 AA across the system. Contrast, measured on the actual backgrounds: #3B2A25 cocoa on peach 12.5:1 and on white 13.6:1; #7A5F56 muted on peach 5.4:1 and on white 5.8:1, so 11px labels pass; cocoa on the #E88C9E rose button 5.6:1 and on pressed #E07F94 4.7:1; cocoa over the peach halftone dots 8.9:1, so the headline stays legible where dots pass behind it; muted text is never set on rose (2.4:1). Pastels never carry text. Interactive dotted borders (ghost button, phone menu disc, time tags) are cocoa at 55% for 3.4:1 against white; the apricot dotted borders (1.8:1) sit only on non-interactive cards. Measured frame: desktop 852px (nav 80 + hero 590 + trust 182); phone primary CTA at about 636px and eligibility at about 698px inside a 760px fold; nothing overflows 1200px or 390px, including the scatter rings. Type floor: 11px for labels and tags, 12px fine print and card copy, 14-18px everything else; nothing is set below 11px. Figure semantics: the megaphone field is a figure with aria-labelledby pointing to a visually hidden figcaption that states the 780 count, the lead, the 8.4% sample click-through and the 5% floor, and that the dots are decorative; every SVG dot field, ring, halftone, confetti and glyph is aria-hidden; the 780, the lead, the 8.4%, the floor label and the stat figures are real DOM text in reading order, so the dot clusters always have a text equivalent; the stat dl keeps dt before dd in the markup and reverses them visually; portrait placeholders carry role='img' with descriptive labels until photographs replace them. Focus: a 2px solid cocoa outline with 3px offset on every link and button via :focus-visible, visible on peach, white and rose, and distinct from the dotted hover ring. Motion: every animation is inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, so reduced-motion users get the finished figure with zero keyframes; nothing autoplays beyond the 1.4s load sequence and nothing loops. Colour is never the only signal: the 5% floor is a cocoa ring plus a label and pointer, filled versus hollow dots mark met versus open, and every dot figure states its number in text. Pointer targets 44px on touch; buttons 48-56px. Headings are sentence case; uppercase is reserved for 11px tracked labels.

heroCopy.eyebrow: One of Google's first nine certified agencies
heroCopy.headline: $10,000 a month, click by click.
heroCopy.sub: Google gives eligible nonprofits $10,000 a month in search ads, and every click is a person already looking for your cause. We acquire the budget, keep it above Google's 5% click-through floor, and send one plain monthly report your board can forward.

signatureMoments: The 780-dot megaphone: one dot per nonprofit client, small at the mouthpiece and large at the bell with a rose lip at the rim, and the named account lead in a pill at the mouthpiece, so the first screen is the client list as a picture plus the person who speaks into it.

The dotted floor line: a sample month's click-through as twenty dots with Google's 5% floor ringed in cocoa at the tenth, under a SAMPLE MONTH tag and one plain sentence about deactivation, so the rule that worries executive directors is drawn, sized and labelled in one card.
Counted stats: $48M+ as 48 apricot dots, the team as 60 blush dots, the 100% guarantee as a butter block with every dot filled, so no number on the site is a claim without its units.

Dots as the whole system: a six-dot cone in the mark, a three-dot glyph on every rose button, dotted leaders under figures, dotted rings around portraits, a three-colour confetti rule between sections and confetti in the page corners, so the site is recognisable at thumbnail size and survives a Webflow edit.
The assembling horn: the dots settle from mouthpiece to bell in 1.2 seconds of pure CSS and then never move again, and under reduced motion the finished figure simply appears.
dependencies: Approve pale peach, cocoa and the four pastels replacing brand blue, and redraw the mark as a cocoa disc holding a six-dot cone; keeping the blue mark would add a colour the system forbids.

Agree the count rule: the hero holds exactly the current client count (780 today) and is regenerated from the script when the number changes, or the caption reads '780 dots as of Sep 2026'; the figure and its caption must never disagree.
Consent from one client for a real redacted month to replace the SAMPLE click-through, or keep the SAMPLE MONTH tag permanently; the hero card never shows unlabelled figures.

Name the account leads publicly and fund a photography half-day for circular colour portraits of Amber Snow, the leads and six to eight team members on a plain peach backdrop; the mockups ship with labelled placeholder discs.

Webflow build with the megaphone and the stat blocks as embed symbols whose inputs are numbers, plus a style-guide page locking the two families, the pill radius, the 14px card radius and the rule that pastels never carry text.
risks: Pastels plus dots can tip into nursery or candy; the direction depends on discipline (generous empty peach, cocoa type everywhere, rose only on the CTA and the rim, no pastel text, one dot figure per screen) and on a locked class set so a later editor cannot add a sixth colour.

780 circles is 28KB of inline SVG and a paint cost on low-end phones; the mockup animates eight groups rather than 780 elements, but production should export the figure as a static SVG asset with the count baked in, and the phone may need a 78-dots-of-ten variant if paint times miss budget.

Rose reads by shape and text, not by edge: cocoa on rose is 5.6:1 but the rose surface is only 2.2:1 against peach, and the apricot card borders are decorative at 1.8:1; the interactive borders are already cocoa at 55%, and any new control must follow that rule.

Dropping brand blue is a visible change for 780 existing clients; the wordmark, favicon, email templates and report PDFs all need the cocoa disc at the same time, and the sales team should expect 'will mine look like that?' about the 8.4% sample.
references: Seurat and Signac (a picture that resolves from dots; warmth from adjacent colours rather than saturation)
Ben-Day and halftone print (dot size as tone, the cheapest way to make one shape read as many)
Headspace (warm pastels and round type kept grown-up by generous space and one dark ink)
Mailchimp's 2018 identity (a hand-assembled system with one ink and pastel tints, no SaaS chrome)
Gabarito and Nunito Sans specimen pages (round geometric display over a soft humanist body)
